what: The learning rule of learn/trainer.py and the hand-over of learn/handover.py, on three cases small enough to work by hand.
how_worked: By hand, on paper, with the sums written in each case's 'worked' lines. No line of learn/ or model/ produced any number here. A weight is written [numerator, denominator]. The quantising rule is the definition's: every weight of the filter times 131071 over the largest magnitude in the set, to the nearest integer, a tie to the even one.

cases.name: one-channel-two-records
worked: Record at 3: signal window frames 3..5 = 4, 3, -1; signal-free window frames 0..2 = 1, -2, 0.
Record at 9: signal window frames 9..11 = 2, 5, -3; signal-free window frames 6..8 = 0, 1, -1.

cases.name: unequal-counts-and-two-ties
worked: The peak is 4. 2 over 4 is one half: 131071 / 2 = 65535.5, an exact tie between 65535 and 65536; the even one is 65536.

-2 over 4: -65535.5, a tie between -65535 and -65536; the even one is -65536. A rule that rounded a tie away from zero gives the same two here; one that rounded a tie toward zero, or downward, does not.

cases.name: three-channels-each-different
worked: A frame is (channel 0, channel 1, channel 2). A sum is written tap by tap, each tap as (channel 0, channel 1, channel 2).
All six weights are one set, and its peak is 10. 6: 786426 / 10 = 78642.6, rounds to 78643. 2: 262142 / 10 = 26214.2, rounds to 26214. 1: 13107.1, rounds to 13107. 10: 131071.
No two channels have the same row, so a rule or a hand-over that exchanged two channels gives other integers.
